title: Natural ordinary quotient Hom comparison for a single pair of modules
statement: Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(A\) a commutative ring, \(J\subseteq A\) an ideal, and \(U\) an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Let \(F_n\) be constant \(A\)-module realization followed by completed scalar extension, restriction to \(U\), and ordinary scalar extension to the \(n\)-th quotient ring: the single-module construction underlying [def-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-model-complexes]. Let \(G\) be additive constant \(A\)-module sections at the slice terminal object and let \(H_n=G\circ(-/J^{n+1}(-))\), using [def-sfb-adic-short-complex-quotient-tower]. There are additive maps \(t_n(M,N):H_n(\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(F_nM,F_nN)\) for all \(A\)-modules \(M,N\). They are natural for arbitrary precomposition \(M'\to M\) and postcomposition \(N\to N'\), are bijective when \(M\) is finite projective, and intertwine \(G\) of the canonical algebraic successor quotient transition with scalar change conjugated by the ordinary module balancing isomorphisms. There are no complexes or degree bounds in this statement.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-adic-perfect-unit-hom] to obtain the additive natural comparisons t with their successor equation and bijectivity for the source A. Keep the same t throughout.

For a finite projective A-module M, choose a splitting from a finite free module, using Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective. Coordinate inclusions and projections give maps i_j:A to M and p_j:M to A with sum_j i_j p_j = id_M. For fixed N, precomposition gives sum_j precomp(p_j) precomp(i_j)=id on Hom_A(M,N). Applying the additive H_n preserves this identity. Applying the additive F_n to the first identity preserves it as well. These identities include the empty rank-zero family.

Injectivity: if t(x)=t(y), naturality for every i_j and the injectivity of t(A,N) imply H_n(precomp(i_j))(x)=H_n(precomp(i_j))(y). Reconstruct x and y with the finite sum identity of step 2. Surjectivity: given y:F_n M to F_n N, choose z_j with t(A,N)(z_j)=y composed with F_n(i_j). Then sum_j H_n(precomp(p_j))(z_j) maps to y by additivity, naturality and the F_n finite sum identity. Thus t(M,N) is bijective. Reuse the unchanged two-variable naturality and successor equations from step 1.

theorem adicPerfectModuleHom (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X) :
    let G := AdicCohomology.sections
      ((coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X).over U) (Over.mk (𝟙 U)) ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat A) AddCommGrpCat
    let H := fun n : ℕ ↦ AdicCohomology.quotient J (n + 1) ⋙ G
    let F := fun n : ℕ ↦ adicPerfectQuotientFunctor X J U n
    ∃ t : ∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A),
        (H n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N)) →+ ((F n).obj M ⟶ (F n).obj N),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A)
        (_ : Module.Finite A M) (_ : Module.Projective A M), Function.Bijective (t n M N)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M M' N N' : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A)
        (a : M' ⟶ M) (b : N ⟶ N') (x : (H n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))),
        t n M' N' ((H n).map (ModuleCat.ofHom
          ((LinearMap.llcomp A M' N N' b.hom).comp (LinearMap.lcomp A N a.hom))) x) =
          (F n).map a ≫ t n M N x ≫ (F n).map b) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A)
        (x : (H (n + 1)).obj (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))),
        t n M N (G.map ((AdicCohomology.transition J
          (Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.le_succ n) 1)).app
            (ModuleCat.of A (M →ₗ[A] N))) x) =
          ((adicPerfectQuotientModuleStep X J U n).app M).inv ≫
            (change (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep X J U n)).map (t (n + 1) M N x) ≫
              ((adicPerfectQuotientModuleStep X J U n).app N).hom)
